blocks.text: Covalent bond do atoms ke beech electrons ki mil kar sharing (mutual sharing) se banta hai. Electrons share karte hue har atom apna valence shell poora kar leta hai aur sab se qareeb noble gas ki configuration pa leta hai. Do Cl atoms ke beech bond ka banna neeche dikhaya gaya hai (Fig. 3.2). Covalent bond non-polar bhi ho sakta hai aur polar bhi. Do Cl atoms ka bond bilkul covalent aur non-polar hai. Dono atoms ki electronegativity bilkul barabar hai, is liye bond wale atoms electrically neutral rehte hain aur kisi atom par charge nahi aata. Aise doosre molecules H₂, F₂, Br₂ aur I₂ hain. Polar covalent bonds ki misalein H–Cl, H–Br, H₂O waghaira hain.

blocks.alt: Do chlorine atoms (2, 8, 7) ke shell diagrams, aik ke electrons crosses aur doosre ke dots. Woh aapas mein milte hain aur har aik ka aik electron beech sanjha hota hai (shared pair); ab Cl2 mein har atom ke bahar aath electrons hain.

blocks.prompt: Br₂ ka bond non-polar aur H–Br ka bond polar kyun hai, jabke dono covalent hain?
blocks.explanation: Br₂ mein dono atoms ek jaise hain aur un ki electronegativity barabar hai, is liye shared pair beech mein rehta hai aur kisi atom par charge nahi aata. H–Br mein bromine hydrogen se zyada electronegative hai, woh shared pair ko apni taraf khinchta hai, is liye bond par partial charges aa jate hain aur bond polar ban jata hai.

items: Covalent bond: electrons ki sharing, taake har atom noble gas configuration paye; electronegativity barabar ho to non-polar (Cl₂, H₂, F₂, Br₂, I₂), alag ho to polar (H–Cl, H–Br, H₂O).
